en: The catalog of newly transcribed and invited dharma-gates and so forth consists of those items not previously included in the Tōji Hōmonroku (Tō-ji Record of Dharma-Gates). In total,
there are one hundred and thirty-four works comprising one hundred and forty-three fascicles, written on a single sheet of paper.
Nineteen sheets.
One fascicle of six rolls of the *Vajraśekhara-yoga-saṃkṣipta-pāṭha-sūtra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra;
two bundles of slips using forty-four sheets of paper. [End of] the *Vajraśekhara-yoga-saṃkṣipta-pāṭha-sūtra*.

One scripture in four fascicles; the translator’s name is not recorded in the old edition, and its text differs slightly from the previously requested scripture. Forty-four sheets of paper. One scripture in two fascicles, the *Vajraśekhara-sūtra: The Heart Mantra Recitation Method of the Lotus Family*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra. Forty-one sheets of paper. *The Ritual for the Extensive Recitation of the Maṇḍala Born of Compassion Entering the Lotus Womb Ocean Assembly from the *Vajraśekhara-sūtra*, in one fascicle, three volumes, translated by Tripiṭaka Master Vajrabodhi; thirty-three folios.
*The Extensive Ritual Manual of the Mahāvairocana-sūtra*, in one fascicle, also titled *The Great Compassionate Womb Treasury*, based on the manuscript of Tripiṭaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha.

The *Dharmapravṛttyācārya-vaṃśa* (The Lineage of the Master Dharmaruci) consists of forty-five folios. The *Susiddhikara-sādhana-pūjāvidhi* (The Ritual for Offerings in the Susiddhikara) in one volume and two fascicles was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha;

its text differs slightly from the previously mentioned *Sūtra on Invoking [Deities]*. It consists of forty-two folios. The *Vajradhātu-yoga-saṃkṣepa-nirdeśa* (A Brief Exposition of Vajradhātu Yoga) in one volume and the *Uṣṇīṣavijaya-yogavidhi* (The Ritual Manual for the Practice of the Uṣṇīṣavijaya Buddha-Crown) in one volume and two fascicles were translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra. These explain the removal of obstacles, the pacification of calamities, the extinction of sins, the protection of the state, the benefiting of living beings, and the realization of Bodhi. They consist of forty-seven folios. The *Uṣṇīṣavijaya-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī* in one volume was translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Vajrabodhi. It explains the extinction of sins, the removal of disasters, the stopping of wind and rain, and the subduing of thieves, and so forth; it consists of three sheets.

One fascicle of the *Vajraśrī-mahāsiddhi-dhāraṇī* (compiled by Cezi); one set of ten fascicles (two fascicles duplicated) of the *Mahābuddhoṣṇīṣa-sūtra* in small characters; one fascicle of the *Mahāvajra-sūtra*, translated by Dharmakṣema and transcribed by Huangfu Zhizhi of Anding across eight sheets; one fascicle of the *Uṣṇīṣa-vṛṣṭi-prārthanā-vidhi* (author unknown) on two sheets, excerpted from miscellaneous texts by Cezi; one fascicle of the *Sarvatathāgata-hṛdaya-prabhāsa-adhiṣṭhāna-bhadrabodhisattvāyur-vardhana-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, translated by Amoghavajra Tripiṭaka Master—this is the same as the previously mentioned *Āyur-vardhana-sūtra*, being a different translation of the same original; four sheets [of the above]; one fascicle of the *Bhadrabodhisattvāyur-vardhana-vajra-parama-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, translated by Amoghavajra Tripiṭaka Master, four sheets; one fascicle of the *Bhadrabodhisattva-vajrasattva-yoga-japa-vidhi*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Great Vast Wisdom (Amoghavajra).

*The Dharma-Wheel of the Great Holy Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva’s Teaching for the Elimination of Calamities Spoken by the Bodhisattva*, in eleven folios; also known as *The Fiery Radiance Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śīlabhadra. *The Teaching for the Elimination of Calamities for Kings and Below, Caused by the Oppression of Malevolent Stars and the Misfortunes of Life-Constellations*, in twelve folios.

*The Sūtra on the Five-Syllable Recitation of Mañjuśrī Yoga*, in one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Vajra. *The Swift Entry into Buddha-Wisdom: Manifesting Buddhahood in the Present*, in seven folios. *The One-Syllable Root Dhāraṇī of Mañjuśrī from the Mahāvaipulya Bodhisattva Piṭaka*, in one fascicle, spoken by an anonymous author.

*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Dharma-Jewel Treasury of Mañjuśrī*, in four folios, concerning the extinction of sins, the removal of illness, and matters such as not conceiving children or conceiving sons; translated by the Tripiṭaka Masters Paramārtha and Ratnabuddhi. *The Reception of the Power of Mantras*.
*The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of Mañjuśrī-kumārabhūta with a Single Topknot (Ekajaṭa), Revealing the Inconceivable Merit of the Holder*:
One fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Vajra-puṇyāyu. *The Attainment of Great Merit*: Five sheets. *The Chapter on the Mantra of the Wordless Heart of Mañjuśrī from the Vajraśekhara*:

One fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Vajra. Contains the Five-Syllable Mantra. Thirteen sheets. *The Mañjuśrī-Yamāntaka-Vajra-Dhāraṇī Sūtra*: One fascicle; spoken by an anonymous author. Subdues and eliminates evil enemies. Great.
*The Ritual Manual for the Ten-Section Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī*, one volume in two fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra;

its efficacy is as described in the original sūtra and cannot be recorded in full here [it occupies thirty-five sheets]. *Sūtra on the Recitation Method of Avalokiteśvara and Tārā Bodhisattva*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra;

twelve sheets. *Sūtra of the Heart Mantra of Avalokiteśvara-Tārā*, one fascicle, author unknown; thirty sheets. *Tārācitta Bodhisattva Dharma*, one fascicle, translated by the Śramaṇa Zhìtōng; it explains the removal of obstacles.

*The Essential Yoga Method of Avalokiteśvara Amoghapāśa Bodhisattva for Accomplishing Siddhi*, not including separate methods; translated by Vajrabodhi; four sheets. *The Single-Seal Method of Avalokiteśvara*, not including separate methods;
translated by Amoghavajra; one scroll; also titled *The Recitation Method of the Heart Mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*; two sheets.
*A Treatise on the Āruli-ka Mantra*, explaining the mantra but omitting its efficacy and ritual applications; it seems incomplete; [concerning] the Blue-Necked Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.

*Sūtra in One Fascicle, Author Unknown* (three pages, accordion-folded booklet): Contains many mantras that do not describe specific ritual functions. *Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Jaleśvara* (one fascicle, author unknown) (one page, accordion-folded booklet):
The *Mahāvidyārāja-mantra* spoken by the Great Yakṣa General Maṇibhadra; it is a mantra of great merit. *Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Parṇaśavarī-Lokeśvara* (translated by Amoghavajra Tripiṭaka Master):

Describes the subduing of the state, the averting of calamities, the elimination of smallpox, pestilence, ghosts, and demons, as well as protective power and the increase [of virtues]; eight pages. Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva...
*The Dharma of the Sādhana of Amoghapāśa*, one fascicle; translator’s name lost; three sheets. *A Brief Ritual Manual for the Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī*, one fascicle; author’s name lost; two sheets.
*The Most Essential Secret Method for the Sequential Recitation of the Universal Wish-Fulfilling Maṇi Cakravartin*, one fascicle;

translated by Śubhakarasiṃha; eight sheets on the method of mental application. *The Extensive Ritual Manual of the Vajrabhairava Assembly: The Supreme Heart Mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Throughout the Three Times*.
One fascicle of a Sūtra translated by Amoghavajra, describing the inconceivable merit of those who practice recitation, which cannot be fully recorded;
one fascicle of the *Qianbi Juntaili* (Thousand-Armed Krodharāja) Dharma, attributed to no specific author, consisting of seventy-four sheets, describing how in the past,
when the celestial hosts were terrified during the battle between the Asura army and the gods, the Buddha commanded Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva to descend.

*The Brief Ritual for Various Dharmas Spoken by Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva to the Army of Asuras, Including the Mantra of Cundī for Summoning and Ceasing Rain*, one fascicle, together with the Sanskrit text, translated by Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra; pure and unadulterated text, eleven sheets.
*The Great Shattering Dhāraṇī for the Swift Accomplishment of Vajra-krodha*, one fascicle, together with the Sanskrit text.

One fascicle translated by Amoghavajra; the *Mahāmegha-vṛṣṭisādhanasūtra* (The Scripture on the Great Cloud Wheel for Invoking Rain), one volume, containing eleven pages of methods for subduing the powerful and sovereign deities and so forth, translated by the Tripitaka Master Amoghavajra, totaling twenty-three pages;
the *Sukhāvatīvyūha-sūtra* (The Amitābha Sūtra) in both Sanskrit and Chinese characters, one fascicle; and the *Lokadhara-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle—these were not [available] to anyone.
The *Six-Leaf Scroll: Discourse on the Sutra of the Rainfall that Fills the Seven-Jeweled Treasury*, translated by Tripiṭaka Master Yi Jing;
the *One-Scroll Leaf: A Separate Ritual for Requesting Rain according to the Dharma*, translated by Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra (one scroll).
This ritual is extremely abbreviated, its procedures are unclear, and it is insufficient due to doubts and omissions. [It lacks] the eight mudrās and ten [mantras] of the *Suvīrapratyaṅgirā*.
*Mahāmudrā*, one fascicle; no commentary recorded; five sheets; describes only the mudrās common to all sections.
*Homa-vidhi-sāra*, one fascicle; no author named; fifteen sheets; explains the ritual procedures for establishing the maṇḍala and performing homa as usual.
*Homa-vidhi*, one fascicle; no author named; eleven sheets; like the *Mahāvairocana Sūtra*, it establishes the Great [Maṇḍala].
*The Ritual for the Empowerment of the Ground for the Maṇḍala*, one fascicle; received by the śramaṇa Yin Xuan, three sheets of text;
contains within it the *Mantra of the Great Yakṣiṇī for Rescuing Urgent Calamities*, as found in the *Mahāvairocana Sūtra*.
*The Ritual Manual for Establishing the Maṇḍala for the Siddhi of the Honored Deity through the Cultivation of Samādhi in the Secret Yoga of the Supreme Vehicle*, one fascicle; by Jñānacakra.
The seven sheets of the transmitted text fully explain the sequential ritual rules. *Mahā-kuṭa-mantra-dharmapada*, one fascicle;
no author’s name, two sheets. A small booklet explaining the mantra for subduing the god Śakra through the great sovereign supernatural powers.
The remainder is the emanation of the Buddha Dīpaṃkara. *Buddhabhāṣita-preta-dāna-mahādhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle; by Baḍa.
*The Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī for Purifying All Eye Diseases and Bestowing Immeasurable Merit, Virtue, and Longevity*, translated by Muke He, twelve pages;
*The Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha through Ānanda When the Buddha’s Own Eyes Could Not See Form*, translated by Amoghavajra Tripiṭaka Master, two pages; *Mārīcī*.

*Devasūtra*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra; three pages; contains the *Sthāpanavidhi-vidhāna* (Ritual Procedures for Establishing the Method) and the *Sarvavighnavinirmukti-kalpa* (Ritual Manual for Avoiding All Difficulties). *Vajrasaṃcaya-guhyadevatā-sūtra*, one fascicle; no author’s name; seven pages.

*Mahesvaradeva-upapatti-mantravidhi* (The Mantra Method for the Spontaneous Birth of the Deity Maheśvara), one fascicle; no author’s name; three pages. *Sthāpanavidhi* (Ritual for Establishing [the Image]).
One fascicle on the Ritual Procedures for the Great Lord Maheśvara’s Dharma of Subduing Enemies and Healing Illnesses through the Practice of Loving-Kindness;
no author is named. Three pages of the Vīnāyaka Rite as Spoken by Cezi, which differs from previous transmissions.
One fascicle on the Nārāyaṇa Method of Battle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Ratnākaraśānti. Three pages of the *Ce* (manual).
The *Subhūti-sūtra on the Subduing of Enemies through Divine Efficacy and the Constant Goddess Kaurī*, one fascicle, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guputa.
Furthermore, the *Method of Talismans for Eliminating All Evil Seeds and Calamities*, five sheets. The above constitutes the second bundle.
*The Sūtra on the Divine Incantation for Dispelling Fever Spoken by the Buddha*: An unnamed author; explains the method for extinguishing fire and feverish ailments; two sheets.

*A Single Volume on the Separate Practice of the Blue-Eyed Celestial Maiden*: An unnamed author; two sheets. *Methods for Subduing Respect and Merit Spoken by Cedi*: Includes incantations and mudrās; one volume of the *Sūtra on the Method of the Goddess Rākā*; translated by a Tripiṭaka Master from Siṃhala; six sheets.
*A Single Volume on the Method of the Goddess Ratnagarbhā Concerning Various Worldly Superior Matters and Supramundane Pure Dharmas Spoken by Cedi*: An unnamed author; two sheets.

One fascicle of the *Dhāraṇī Method of the Four Heavenly Sister Goddesses Spoken by Cedi*, anonymous; six sheets. One fascicle of the *Vināyaka Sūtra Spoken by Cedi* on the Unequal Methods for [Causing] Love, Hatred, Enmity, and Killing among Men and Women;
anonymous; twelve sheets. One fascicle of the *Vijayakumāra Dhāraṇī Sūtra Spoken by Cedi* on Loving Respect, Subduing Enemies, Wealth, Nobility, and the Path of the Rishis;
anonymous; twenty-four sheets. One scroll of the *Separate Ritual Manual for the Sublime Dhāraṇī of Vaiśravaṇa, the Treasure-Treasury Heavenly King*.

One fascicle, translator’s name lost; it explains how one attains great merit. It consists of only seven sheets at the end of the sutra. *The Dharani Method of Vaiśravaṇa, King of the Treasure-Store*, one fascicle;

author’s name lost; six sheets; it explains various distinct methods. *The Sutra of the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa*, one fascicle; translated by Amoghavajra Tripiṭaka Master; includes a preface; seven sheets; it explains the great merit and *siddhi* [accomplishment].
*The Divine and Sublime Chapter of the Dharani of the Treasure-Store Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa*, one fascicle; translated by Dharmagana; six sheets; explained in a memorandum.

*The Ritual for the Eight World-Protecting Devas (Lokapālas) for Bestowing Love, Increasing [Prosperity], Subduing Enemies, Ceasing Rain, and Overpowering Heretics, Granting Longevity, and Attaining the Threefold Siddhi*, one fascicle;
compiled by the Śramaṇa Faquan of Qinglong Monastery, six sheets. At the end of this scroll, there is a detailed explanation of the sequence of the ten titles of the Tathāgata in Sanskrit characters.

*The Sūtra of Miscellaneous Secret Mantras of the Garuḍa King*, one fascicle; translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Prajñā of Kaśmīra, twenty-five sheets. It explains the elimination of poisons, the treatment of diseases, and various secret mantras of the nāgas contained herein. *The Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra-rāja*.
One scroll of *Mantra* (containing both Sanskrit and Chinese characters); no compiler’s name; sixteen sheets. One scroll of the *Uṣṇīṣavijaya-dhāraṇī* in Sanskrit characters;
the script differs slightly. One scroll of miscellaneous *mantras* in Sanskrit characters; no compiler’s name; nineteen sheets. Thirty-five Buddha names in Sanskrit characters.
Twenty-six *yakṣa* generals, each with their respective *mantras*. The *Amitābha-mahātejas-amṛta-padma-rāja-kuṇḍalī-mantra*. Threefold *dhāraṇīs*. Threefold Bodhi-ornamentation Great Vajra.
*The Dhāraṇī of Exultation*, one fascicle; *The Discourse on Loving-Kindness, Wealth, and Nobility*, one line;

*The Commentary on the Verses of the Boundless Nectar Dhāraṇī of the Great General Aṭavaka, an Emanation of Bodhisattva Akṣayamati*, one fascicle, translated by Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra, three sheets;

*The Commentary on the Cintāmaṇicakra Dhāraṇī*, one sheet, annotated by Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra; *The Sūtra of the Heart of the Siddham Song of Praise*, one fascicle, translated by Buddhapālita, six sheets; *The Great Vairocana Tathāgata...* [text continues].

One fascicle of the *Bai-tai-zang-man-tu-lo-zan* (Praise of the Compassionate Garbha Maṇḍala), consisting of three sheets of Sanskrit and Chinese characters in a small-format scroll; one manuscript in Sanskrit characters of the *Da-pi-lu-cha-na-pu-gong-yang-zan* (Praise of the Universal Offering to Mahāvairocana);

one fascicle of the *Da-pi-lu-cha-na-ru-lai-puti-xin-zan* (Praise of the Bodhicitta of Tathāgata Mahāvairocana); and one fascicle of the *Da-pi-lu-cha-na-ru-lai-lüe-zan* (Brief Praise of Tathāgata Mahāvairocana). The above two praises comprise one sheet.

One fascicle of the *Jingangding-baobu-shiliuzun-zan* (Praise of the Sixteen Honored Ones of the Vajraśekhara Jewel Family). The *Jingangbu-zan* (Praise of the Vajra Family) is contained within the *Dayi-guiju* (Great Ritual Manual) and comprises two sheets. One hundred [verses] of the Vajraśekhara Lotus Family...

1. *Praise in One Hundred and Eight Names* (one fascicle, two sheets, palm-leaf manuscript), Vajrapadma-kula. 2. *Praise in One Hundred and Eight Names* (one fascicle, two sheets, palm-leaf manuscript), Vajraśekhara-karmakula.
The above six major praises constitute one combined volume in Sanskrit script. 3. *Praise in One Hundred and Eight Names of Trailokyavijaya* (one fascicle, one sheet, palm-leaf manuscript). 4.
*Praise for Petitioning the Great Maṇḍala* (one fascicle, one sheet, palm-leaf manuscript, in Sanskrit script). 5. *Buddha-sahasrāra-cakra-stotra* (one fascicle, six lines, in Sanskrit script).
*Praise of the Seven Buddhas*, one fascicle; *Threefold Miscellaneous Praises*, three sheets; *Praise of the Triple Gem by Chang Ce-zi*, one fascicle; miscellaneous praises and others, four sheets;

*Praise of the One Hundred and Eight Names of Mañjuśrī*, one fascicle, two sheets; *Praise of the Mother of the Seven Koṭis of Buddhas, the Cundi*, one volume, one sheet; *Heart Dhāraṇī of the Thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa*, one volume, one sheet;

*The Sixteen Honored Ones and the Twenty Devas of the Bhadrakalpa along with their Mantras*, one fascicle, two sheets; *Mantra of the Buddha’s Footprints*, one character in Sanskrit script, two [sheets].
One fascicle of the *Mahānīlanbara-vajra-mantra* in Sanskrit characters, one sheet per fascicle; one fascicle of the *Mahānīlamukha-mahāvajra-harṣa-mantra*, one sheet per fascicle;

one fascicle of the *Karuṇāpuṇya-mayūra-vidyārāja-sūtra* with the extremely abbreviated ritual and diagrams, anonymous; this method is a concise summary, and its altar deities differ from those previously mentioned;
